patch_description: Instead of random points, I use a structured ansatz: 12 points near the boundary of a triangle-ish/square convex region plus interior points, then run a deterministic greedy local search (coordinate perturbation with shrinking step) that directly maximizes the smallest triangle area over all 286 triangles. The key insight: near-optimal Heilbronn configurations put most points on the convex hull boundary, since boundary points only form triangles with two others and thus relieve crowding. The search starts from a ring + center configuration, evaluates all triangle areas vectorized, and greedily accepts improvements until convergence, guaranteeing determinism and a much larger min-area than random sampling.
